name: Overtime on a weekday, a rest day and a holiday, with night hours
source: synthetic — replace with anonymised real cases
derivation: Base 22,000,000, 22 working days, 8 hours a day: the hourly rate is 22,000,000 / (22 x 8 = 176) = 125,000 exactly.
The policy multiplies the base salary only (overtimeBase = base_salary).

Weekday overtime 120 minutes at night: the multiplier is 150% + 30% night premium + 20% extra for overtime at night = 200%; 125,000 x (120 x 200) / 6000 = 125,000 x 4 = 500,000. OT_WEEKDAY = 2,375,000.
Ordinary hours worked inside the night window: 180 minutes x 30% premium = 125,000 x (180 x 30) / 6000 = 112,500.

PIT exemption, seeded mode 'premium_only': only what exceeds ordinary-hours pay is exempt. The same overtime hours at 100% would be weekday 125,000 x (720 x 100)/6000 = 1,500,000, rest day 125,000 x (480 x 100)/6000 = 1,000,000, holiday 125,000 x (240 x 100)/6000 = 500,000 — together 3,000,000. The night premium on ordinary hours is pure premium, so all of it is exempt.
Insurance on 22,000,000 (overtime is never in the contribution base): employee 1,760,000 + 330,000 + 220,000 = 2,310,000; employer 3,850,000 + 660,000 + 220,000 = 4,730,000.
